title: Adding and Subtracting Integers
seo_title: Grade 7 Adding and Subtracting Integers Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 7)
standard_text: Add and subtract integers; using concrete models (e.g., counters, integer chips), pictorial models (e.g., bar models, number lines), and with integers written as numerals.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 adding and subtracting integers worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: integer chips, number lines, rules for signs and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Different signs: subtract and keep the sign of the larger absolute value.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • With integer chips, a positive and a negative chip make a zero pair.
  • Same signs: add the absolute values and keep the sign. −4 + (−6) = −10.
  • Different signs: subtract the absolute values and keep the sign of the one farther from 0. −9 + 5 = −4.
  • To subtract, add the opposite: 3 − (−5) = 3 + 5 = 8.

Examples

Example

−7 − (−10)

−7 + 10

Answer: 3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when signs differ−9 + 5 is −4, not −14.
− (−) as negativeSubtracting −5 is adding 5.
Wrong signKeep the sign of the number farther from 0.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 7 ask about adding integers?
faq.a: Add and subtract integers using concrete models (integer chips), pictorial models (bar models, number lines), and with integers written as numerals.
One positive and one negative chip, which add to 0.

faq.q: How do I check an answer?
faq.a: Add the answer to the number you subtracted.

items.q: A yellow tile is +1 and a red tile is −1. What integer do these tiles show?
items.e: Each yellow and red pair is a zero pair: 1 + (−1) = 0. There are 2 zero pairs. Remove them: 4 yellow tiles are left. The tiles show 4.

items.q: Which addition do these tiles show?

items.q: Which addition do these tiles show?
items.e: The first group has 7 yellow tiles, so it is 7. The second group has 3 red tiles, so it is −3. The tiles show 7 + (−3).

items.q: Vincent models −7 + 3 with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: Make 3 zero pairs and remove them. 4 red tiles are left. Different signs: subtract the sizes, 7 − 3 = 4. −7 is farther from 0, so the answer is negative. −7 + 3 = −4.

items.q: Angelo models 4 + (−9) with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: Make 4 zero pairs and remove them. 5 red tiles are left. Different signs: subtract the sizes, 9 − 4 = 5. −9 is farther from 0, so the answer is negative. 4 + (−9) = −5.

items.q: Carmela models −2 + (−5) with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: All the tiles are red, so there are no zero pairs. Count them: 7 red tiles. −2 + (−5) = −7.

items.q: Christian models 8 + (−3) with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: Make 3 zero pairs and remove them. 5 yellow tiles are left. Different signs: subtract the sizes, 8 − 3 = 5. 8 is farther from 0, so the answer is positive. 8 + (−3) = 5.

items.q: Renz models −6 + 6 with tiles. What is the sum?
items.e: Make 6 zero pairs and remove them. No tiles are left, so the sum is 0. A number plus its opposite is always 0.

items.q: Janelle wants to show −2 with integer tiles. She starts with 6 red tiles. How many yellow tiles does she need to add?
items.e: The 6 red tiles show −6. Each yellow tile you add makes a zero pair with a red tile and raises the value by 1. To get to −2, add 4 yellow tiles: −6 + 4 = −2.

items.q: Lorna shows an integer with 3 yellow tiles and 11 red tiles. What integer is it?
items.e: 3 zero pairs are worth 0. The other 8 red tiles are worth −8. So 3 yellow tiles and 11 red tiles show 3 + (−11) = −8.

items.q: Without calculating, what can you say about −53 + 38?
c: It is negative, because −53 is farther from 0.
It is positive, because 53 + 38 is positive.
It is negative, because both numbers are negative.
It is positive, because 38 is positive.
items.e: The signs are different, so the sum has the sign of the number farther from 0. 53 > 38, so the sum is negative (it is −15).

items.q: Joshua is diving at −7 m and Jenny is diving at −19 m. How far apart are they?
items.e: Subtract the positions: −7 − (−19) = −7 + 19 = 12 m. Both are below the surface, so the distance is 19 − 7.

items.q: In a class quiz game, a right answer is +10 points and a wrong answer is −15 points. A team has −25 points and then gets one wrong answer. What is the team’s score now?
items.e: A wrong answer adds −15: −25 + (−15) = −40.

items.q: In volleyball, a player’s plus-minus goes up 1 when the player’s team scores while the player is on the ice, and down 1 when the other team scores. Gabriel’s plus-minus is 2. In the next game, his team scores 1 goal and the other team scores 4 while he is on the ice. What is his plus-minus now?
items.e: The change is 1 + (−4) = −3. Then 2 + (−3) = −1.
